subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What supported OpenClaw API should represent Telegram custom emoji: a shared Markdown/IR custom-emoji span, Telegram-specific `entities` / `caption_entities` in channel data, or raw `<tg-emoji>` HTML only?
rationale: Current source can preserve raw HTML but cannot carry first-class entity metadata through the shared message tool; adding that surface changes public message-tool/plugin contracts and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Add typed entity support
options.body: Expose a narrow, validated Telegram entity/caption-entity payload through the message tool and Telegram plugin, with UTF-16 offset validation and delivery tests.

options.title: Design shared IR first
options.body: Add a cross-channel custom emoji span to the Markdown/message presentation model before Telegram-specific send wiring, trading broader architecture for a cleaner long-term abstraction.

options.title: Keep raw HTML only
options.body: Document `<tg-emoji>` as the supported escape hatch and close first-class entity support as out of scope, leaving plugin slash-command entity arrays unsupported.

recommendation.title: Add typed entity support
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow, validated Telegram entity/caption-entity payload through the message tool and Telegram plugin, with UTF-16 offset validation and delivery tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the most concrete maintainer-facing review of the API-shape blocker and has adjacent Telegram command-runtime history.
